I'm coming to accept it- a lot of people just don't like glute-ham raises. Some people say they hurt their feet, some people say they can't really feel their glutes working and that it's more of a hamstring isolation exercises than anything, and some people just can't find a place to do them without breaking anything. Personally I think they're a great exercise, but we all experience the world differently, and what is a great exercise for me might be a terrible one for someone else. So, in the spirit of the versatility and minimalism of bodyweight training, I bring you an alternative, one that you can do anywhere without fear of breaking anything, and that will blast your glutes as much if not more than your hammies, just in case they weren't getting enough work from the shrimp squat progression already. [for the record, glute-ham raises or "nordic leg curls" ARE a glute exercise- if you bend at the waist the glutes actively assist in the motion, and even if you keep your body perfectly straight all the time, they are worked isometrically anyways.]

This alternative exercise I'm speaking of is the sliding bridge curl, and all that you need to do it is a floor and something that slides on that floor. Either some rags and a hard floor, or some furniture sliders and carpet. The progression isn't quite as simple as the glute-ham raise progression is, but it's not convoluted either. I'll lay it out here in steps.

Step 1 [very easy]- do a regular, unweighted glute bridge with your feet on the towels/sliders, and then do a sliding eccentric to a lying position to hit the hamstrings. Reset and repeat for reps.

Step 2 [easy]- start in the lying down position with the sliders under your feet, curl yourself up to the glute bridge position, slide back down, and repeat for reps. [I do these for high reps sometimes, they give me a killer gluteal pump, which I strangely enjoy.]

Step 3 [medium]- just like step 2 but with a one-leg eccentric. Alternate legs, of course. You don't want uneven buttcheeks.

Step 4 [medium-difficult]- do a one-legged glute bridge with a one-legged sliding eccentric. Do one leg for reps, then the other for reps.

Step 5 [difficult]- do one-leg sliding bridge curls! Pretty killer. All unilateral bodyweight movements work the core, but with this one you'll really feel it.

So there you go, people who don't like or can't do glute-ham raises but still want to get nice glutes and hamstrings with bodyweight. Now you know how.

This has been Demonic_Mime, and I'm out.
A replacement for the glute-ham raises in the beginner routine - for people who don't like them, or can't find a place to do them
